block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Family fit depends on the home and the surrounding daily routine. For luxury buyers, compare layout, storage, parking, privacy, noise, commute, amenities, community maturity and the practical needs of the household. A strong sales or investment narrative does not compensate for a home that works poorly in everyday use.

items.answer: Family fit depends on the home and the surrounding daily routine. For luxury buyers, map work, school, shopping, leisure and transport needs against how the property and location would actually be used each week.
items.question: How should I assess whether a property suits a family buyer?

items.answer: End-user fit is mainly about how well the property supports everyday life. Compare room sizes, storage, outdoor space, parking and privacy with the household requirements rather than relying on bedroom count alone.
items.question: How should I assess whether a property suits an end-user buyer?

items.answer: A branded residence is worthwhile only when the underlying property justifies the premium. Test whether the layout, view, location, specification or service offer is genuinely difficult to replicate in competing developments.
items.question: How should I assess whether a branded residence fits my needs?

items.answer: Luxury fit depends on scarcity, quality and buyer relevance rather than price alone. Consider how many future buyers may value the same premium and whether resale depends on a narrow luxury or brand-sensitive audience.
items.question: How should I assess whether a luxury property fits my needs?

items.answer: A floor plan should be judged by usable space, not only total area. Corridors, awkward corners or oversized circulation reduce the usable value of the stated size. Compare plans at similar sizes because two units with the same area can function very differently.
